evidence: The actual frozen workbook quality row 38 (sheet row 39) and its internal annotation require independent per-criterion verdicts and continuation after a failure; gate dimensions are exempt. Manual source review confirms all three scored prompts satisfy this: task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:9 says "score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure, and preserve successful observations" and prohibits inheriting sibling verdicts, with alternate minimal setup when prerequisites fail. Its lines 34,39,50,52 give concrete fallback/preservation instructions for unusual-ID routing, chain failures, concurrent operations and restart. task/tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:6 says "judge each criterion independently, continue after failures and preserve valid observations"; lines 8-10 preserve independent form recovery and allow alternate eligible targets. task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:6 says "grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures"; line 8 prohibits deducting one defect repeatedly under renamed properties. Injected app_context.md adds no contradictory stop rule. The frozen template matches the intended policy at functional/prompt.md:68-69, polish/prompt.md:16-20 and visual/prompt.md:46-49; the permitted global browser gate remains separate. All referenced task, workbook, skill/reference and template hashes were checked against manifest.json and matched, including scored prompt SHA256 functional=700ce0cd545a21a18727ca13ef66a9bb250db424f951fefa6c4b64a987e56419, polish=c1b99fea66673d61cdf8084434b8c64765aa95029d2e82144cd93243d5711465, visual=2161fddcad10140328b5deb4d603a6505b9e70997769e1c29f361e130bd7430a, workbook=6d44970b2ff67fefad1e2327e743fc226fcd4c50ff55baf899f41069a9b3fd7f. This is a source-wording finding, not a private checker execution or configured-judge measurement; runtime grading behavior remains unmeasured here.
counterexample: Source-level adversarial checks, not app executions: a broken app that lacks dark mode but supports keyboard/mobile cannot be credited by a sibling pass and cannot have all Polish rows zeroed by that one miss (polish prompt line 6). A conforming custom route/layout app, or a partially conforming app whose unusual-ID chain fails while ordinary operations work, is protected by intent-based navigation and ordinary-ID fallback (functional lines 11 and 34). No stop-on-first-failure rule or shared verdict was found in the assigned-row evidence.
